summary: A room's culture account is no longer refused for being slightly long, and the fold can look up three times as many people before it writes.
details: The culture fold refused any account over 1,400 characters, and 6 of 11 live draws were over it. A refused draw spends a model call and re-folds the same batch, so the deployment's busiest room paid four before a fifth came in under the cap and recorded. The cap is 20,000 now and is a corruption ceiling rather than a quality judgement.

The cap no longer sizes the fold's token budgets. Those are sized on what the model has actually been observed to emit, so raising the refusal threshold no longer demands a completion ceiling nothing would use.

The culture fold and the proactive pass may each make three times as many person lookups before deciding - 12 rather than 4, with the shared per-pass memory ceiling raised alongside so the rise is not inert.
limitations: Nothing automatically refuses an account that has drifted back into chronicle. That guard belongs to the objective's own instruction, which is operator-owned and needs its eval arm; the character cap was never able to do it.
